Looking for Philippines-based candidates

Job Role: Apparel Designer

Compensation Range: $1,500 USD / Monthly

Engagement Type:Independent Contractor Agreement

Work Schedule: This role is expected to align with the client’s US business hours (approx. 9 AM - 5 PM, Monday to Friday, EST) for collaboration, but as a contractor, you’ll have flexibility in how you manage your time.

Who We Are: At Hunt St, we help Australian and US companies hire top remote talent in the Philippines. For this role, you will be engaged directly by the client as an independent contractor. We are not an outsourcing agency. All of our roles are 100% remote so you'll be able to work from home.

Who The Client Is: Our client is an established and rapidly growing apparel business with over 30 years of experience in the fashion industry. The company specializes in designing and developing trend-driven clothing and lifestyle products for some of the largest retail businesses in the United States.

With extensive industry experience, established retail partnerships, and a strong focus on product development, the business continues to expand its collections and brand portfolio.

Role Overview: We are looking for an experienced, creative, and technically skilled Apparel Designer to join the team and contribute to the development of its growing product range as the company enters its next phase of growth.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Design and develop apparel collections for Baby Phat, Paul Frank, and other company brands.
  • Create complete, factory-ready tech packs independently, including detailed specifications, measurements, construction details, trims, fabrics, colors, artwork placement, and finishing requirements.
  • Develop accurate technical flat sketches and CAD presentations using Adobe Illustrator.
  • Create detailed size specifications, measurement charts, and grading instructions.
  • Review samples, fittings, and production details to ensure accuracy and quality.
  • Communicate technical corrections and revisions directly with overseas factories.
  • Research current fashion trends, fabrics, silhouettes, prints, and graphics.
  • Develop new concepts and designs appropriate for major national retail chains.
  • Create colorways, print layouts, graphic placements, and presentation boards.
  • Work closely with merchandising, sales, and production teams to bring collections from initial concept through final production.
  • Manage multiple styles and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

Required Skills and Qualifications:

  • 5–10 years of professional apparel design experience required.
  • Strong experience creating and developing complete, production-ready tech packs specifically for the US junior apparel market, with an understanding of its target audience, sizing, fit, and fashion trends is essential.
  • Advanced proficiency in Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop.
  • Strong technical knowledge of garment construction, fabrics, trims, measurements, and fit.
  • Ability to create professional CADs, technical flats, and detailed specification sheets.
  • Experience communicating directly with overseas factories and reviewing production samples.
  • Understanding of apparel manufacturing and production processes.
  • Strong knowledge of current fashion trends and commercial retail design.
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to work independently, manage multiple projects, and meet tight deadlines.
  • Previous experience designing for major retailers, licensed brands, or private-label apparel is highly desirable.
  • Experience with women's sportswear, casualwear, fleece, knits, and graphic apparel is a plus.

Why Join Us?

  • Work with iconic licensed brands including Baby Phat and Paul Frank.
  • Be part of a rapidly expanding apparel business with established national retail distribution.
  • See your designs go from initial concept to finished products sold at major retail chains.
  • Work directly with an experienced team with over 30 years of industry expertise.
  • Have meaningful creative involvement and responsibility in developing new collections.
  • Join a company where creativity, technical skills, and the ability to get things done are valued.

Work Arrangement & Expectations:

This is a remote role that will be set up as an independent contractor engagement.

To ensure alignment and transparency, successful candidates will be expected to:

  • Disclose any existing ongoing roles or client work
  • Reflect this engagement on their LinkedIn profile (clearly marked as “Independent Contractor”)

Role Purpose

Develop foundational Apparel Engineering capability while supporting the technical development, sample review and production readiness of assigned apparel products. Working under the guidance of experienced Apparel Engineers and managers, the role applies established standards, builds practical knowledge across product categories and supports timely, accurate physical and digital development for compressed Go-To-Market calendars. Develop effective working relationships within VF pillars, with Brand and factory partners by communicating clearly, following through on commitments, asking questions and contributing positively to shared product outcomes.


Key Accountabilities

1. Product Development Support

  • Learn and apply established Apparel Engineering standards, tools and processes to assigned products and development activities.
  • Support Brand Development, Sourcing Development and vendors with routine technical follow-up across development and commercialization stages.
  • Assist with fit, pattern, construction, measurement, material and manufacturing reviews, documenting observations and proposed actions for review by an experienced Apparel Engineer.
  • Support construction, sizing, grading and block-related activities within clearly defined instructions and scope.
  • Raise unclear, complex, high-risk or material issues promptly rather than resolving them independently.

2. Physical & Digital Sample Support

  • Support the review of physical and digital samples across relevant development stages, including Proto, SMS, POC, PPS, Counter and Size Set.
  • Check assigned samples against the Tech Pack, measurements, approved product intent and established construction and workmanship standards.
  • Prepare clear draft comments, measurements, images and supporting information for review and approval by an experienced Apparel Engineer where required.
  • Update sample records, forms and systems accurately and on time, maintaining alignment between physical and digital findings.
  • Follow up with vendor technical teams on agreed actions and escalate late, repeated or unresolved issues.

3. Risk, Testing & Production Readiness Support

  • Support product risk classification and monitoring using established RBM guidance and direction from the Manager or Senior Apparel Engineer.
  • Prepare information for Tech Pack handover, Risk Analysis handoff, PRM, PP meetings, and participate as required.
  • Identify and record Tech Pack discrepancies; update minor discrepancies only where authorized and escalate all material or unclear items.
  • Coordinate assigned testing activities and track results, failures and agreed corrective actions under guidance.
  • Support production-readiness checks by confirming that assigned actions, sample comments and technical information are complete and current.

4. Learning, Cross-Category Growth & Development Trips

  • Build technical capability through intentional learning and planned exposure across product categories, manufacturing methods and development stages.
  • Participate in technical calibration, coaching, knowledge-sharing and training, and maintain an active Individual Development Plan.

5. Factory Exposure & Partner Support

  • Travel to factories as required to gain hands-on exposure to product development and manufacturing, support sample and product reviews, and develop effective working relationships with CFT and wider factory pattern and digital specialists teams.
  • Observe factory processes, sample-room practices and production methods to strengthen practical understanding of how technical decisions affect execution.
  • Support CFT and factory partners by providing accurate information, following up agreed actions and escalating questions that require more experienced technical judgment.
  • Participate in vendor training, TVCP, CFT correlation and RBM calibration activities as a learner and contributor under guidance.

6. Collaboration & Ways of Working

  • Work collaboratively with brands, vendors, CFT, factory teams and regional Apparel Engineering colleagues within the assigned scope.
  • Communicate progress, questions, delays and risks clearly and early.
  • Support updates to construction tools, manuals, SOPs and standardized VF Way processes by completing assigned research, documentation or system updates.
  • Participate in team projects and continuous-improvement activities, contributing observations and learning from assigned work.

Success Profile

Core Competencies

  • Growth mindset, curiosity and willingness to learn through coaching, feedback and hands-on experience.
  • Attention to detail, good organization and reliable follow-through on assigned actions.
  • Ability to work within established processes, manage priorities and meet agreed calendar deadlines.
  • Collaborative and respectful approach when working with cross-functional and factory partners.
  • Clear verbal and written communication, active listening and confidence to ask questions.
  • Ability to recognize limits of knowledge and escalate issues appropriately.
  • Interest in developing technical breadth across apparel product categories.

Foundational Technical Skills & Knowledge

  • Foundational understanding of apparel product development, garment construction, patterns, measurements, fit and manufacturing.
  • Ability to read and interpret basic Tech Packs, technical sketches, measurement specifications and sample comments.
  • Basic practical exposure to pattern making, apparel sizing, grading, live-model fitting or body-form fitting through education, training or work experience.
  • Familiarity with relevant digital tools such as Gerber, Flex or another PLM system, Browzwear or another 3D apparel tool, and Adobe Illustrator is beneficial; training may be provided based on business needs.
  • Basic understanding of raw-material behavior, wet processing, garment testing and apparel manufacturing methods is beneficial.
  • Ability to compare samples with defined standards, document findings accurately and support straightforward problem-solving.

Education, Experience & Language

  • A relevant degree, diploma or recognized technical training up to 3 years in apparel engineering, garment technology, technical design, pattern making, fashion technology, textile technology or a related discipline is preferred.
  • Recent graduates and early-career candidates may be considered where they demonstrate strong technical fundamentals, learning agility, attention to detail and genuine interest in apparel engineering.
  • Relevant internship, placement, sample-room, pattern, fit, product-development or manufacturing experience is beneficial but not essential.
  • English and relevant local language.

Role Scope & Decision Authority

  • Entry-level Individual Contributor with no direct people-management or formal technical-leadership accountability.
  • Works within established standards, defined assignments and delegated authority, with coaching and review from experienced Apparel Engineers and managers.
  • Does not independently own complex or high-risk product decisions, vendor performance management, technical capability programs or major cross-functional workstreams.
  • Does not have responsibility for SMV / YY exception validation.
  • Progressively takes on broader product scope and greater independence as technical capability and judgment develop.

Help empower our global customers to connect to culture through their passions.

Why you’ll love this role:

StockX is the world’s leading marketplace for current culture, built at the intersection of commerce, community, and credibility. Apparel is foundational to StockX — not just as a category, but as an expression of identity, culture, and global trends.

We are expanding how apparel culture shows up on StockX through creator-driven, community-oriented commerce experiences that blend storytelling, expertise, and transaction. To do this well, we need category leaders who don’t just understand the apparel market — they live inside it.

The Apparel Category Manager is the single-threaded owner of apparel category growth within a new, high-priority commerce initiative. This person is the in-house expert on Fashion & Apparel culture, people, economics, and moments — and is responsible for translating that expertise into supply growth, engagement, and GMV.

You will act as:

  • The internal authority on the first-hand and second-hand apparel ecosystem
  • The external face of StockX to apparel sellers, creators, designers, and community leaders
  • The architect of the apparel go-to-market playbook for this new initiative

This role blends deep cultural fluency, strategic ownership, and hands-on execution. Early on, you will own everything related to apparel within this initiative. As the category scales, you will grow into a leader overseeing a broader apparel portfolio and team.

What You’ll Do:

Own the Apparel Category End-to-End

  • Define and execute the growth strategy for apparel within the platform
  • Own category-level performance across supply, engagement, and revenue
  • Establish quarterly goals, leading indicators, and operating rhythms

Be the Market & Culture Expert

  • Maintain deep, current knowledge of apparel culture, including:
    • Key sellers, creators, designers, brands, and retailers
    • Sub-segments (streetwear, luxury, contemporary, vintage, performance, regional styles, etc.)
    • Seasonal drops, brand dynamics, collaborations, and cultural moments
    • Pricing dynamics, liquidity, and resale economics
  • Serve as the internal voice of the apparel community, informing product, marketing, and platform decisions

Supply & Creator Acquisition

  • Build and own a pipeline of high-impact apparel sellers, shops, designers, influencers, brands, and creators
  • Personally recruit and onboard flagship sellers who set the tone for the platform
  • Develop seller strategies that balance credibility, storytelling, and commerce

Commerce Strategy & Category Moments

  • Identify and orchestrate Fashion & Apparel-specific moments, campaigns, and formats that drive engagement and conversion
  • Partner with Category Marketing to design culturally authentic activations
  • Experiment with new approaches and iterate quickly based on performance and feedback

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Work closely with Account and Partnerships Managers to scale seller acquisition and support
  • Collaborate with Product and Engineering to shape features and tools that matter to category sellers and buyers
  • Provide clear, actionable insights from the market to influence roadmap prioritization

Build the Playbook

  • Document learnings, frameworks, and best practices that can be reused across future categories
  • Help define what “great” looks like for category ownership at StockX
  • Support hiring and onboarding as the apparel category team grows

About you:

  • Deeply embedded in second-hand fashion & apparel culture — you know the people, platforms, trends, and economics, and you’re already plugged into the ecosystem
  • 5+ years of experience in category management, partnerships, marketplace growth, brand, or operator roles in apparel, streetwear, fashion, or adjacent ecosystems
  • Comfortable owning outcomes, not just strategy — you execute, iterate, and adapt
  • Strong relationship builder with credibility among sellers, creators, designers, and community members
  • Data-literate and commercially minded — you understand pricing, margins, liquidity, and incentives
  • Entrepreneurial, scrappy, and energized by building something from the ground up

Nice to Have:

  • Existing network of apparel resellers, brand operators, designers, boutiques, or creators
  • Experience buying and selling apparel or operating within resale or fashion marketplaces
  • Familiarity with content-driven commerce, creator platforms, or enthusiast communities
  • Experience working cross-functionally with product and engineering teams
  • Experience running your own business or startup

Why This Role Matters:

Apparel will define the early perception and success of this new commerce initiative at StockX. This role sets:

  • The cultural bar for the platform
  • The go-to-market blueprint for future categories
  • The credibility of StockX with the apparel community

You will have outsized influence on how StockX expands its leadership from marketplace into deeper cultural engagement.

StockX is proud to be a Detroit-based technology leader focused on the large and growing online market for sneakers, apparel, accessories, electronics, collectibles, trading cards, and more. This approach affords access and market visibility powered by real-time data that empowers buyers and sellers to determine and transact based on market value. The StockX platform features hundreds of brands across verticals including Jordan Brand, adidas, Nike, Supreme, BAPE, Off-White, Louis Vuitton, Gucci; collectibles from brands including LEGO, KAWS, Bearbrick, and Pop Mart; and electronics from industry-leading manufacturers Sony, Microsoft, Meta, and Apple.   • Knowledge of fabrics, fibers, weaves, knits, printing techniques, and finishes.

  • Comfortable working with physical samples, measurements, and multiple rounds of revisions.

  • Strong eye for color, trends, and what sells.

About the role
Staff Accountant

We are hiring on behalf of a fast-growing DTC men's apparel brand doing over $10M per month in revenue. Comfort-first, performance-minded basics: shorts, tees, hoodies, pants. California-rooted, 100% bootstrapped, running on Shopify with paid Meta as the growth engine.

The Role

This is not a back-office job. This is the financial nerve center of a fast-moving DTC operation.

You will own the daily accounting engine covering AP, receiving reconciliation, vendor accounts, and COGS accuracy. Then you will do what most accountants cannot: turn those numbers into answers. Which SKUs are printing money and which are dead weight? Which vendors are quietly bleeding the company on variances?

You will work directly with ownership. No layers, no bureaucracy. Ownership handles month-end close and the big strategic calls. You run the daily operation, surface what matters, and bring analysis sharp enough to change decisions. When you find something, it gets acted on that day.

If you have ever caught a six-figure error nobody else saw, or built the analysis that killed a bad product line, this is your room.

What You'll Own

Accounts Payable, full cycle

  • Process, code, and schedule vendor invoices across the full supplier base
  • Execute 3-way matching (PO, receiving report, invoice) on every inbound shipment
  • Run payment cycles, track terms, and capture early-pay discounts
  • Resolve discrepancies directly with vendors

Receiving and Inventory Accuracy

  • Daily reconciliation of invoiced quantities against goods actually received
  • Catch short ships, production variances, and pricing errors before they become write-offs
  • Partner with fulfillment leadership to keep receiving documentation airtight

COGS and Unit Economics

  • Maintain weighted average cost accuracy across roughly 1,300 SKUs
  • Reconcile landed costs including freight, duties, and inbound charges into true unit economics
  • Support monthly COGS true-ups and inventory valuation reviews

Vendor Management

  • Own vendor account reconciliations, statement reviews, and terms compliance
  • First line on anything billing-related with the supplier network
  • Track vendor performance: variance rates, pricing drift, chargeback recovery

Analysis

  • Blended and category-level gross margin tracking
  • SKU contribution, velocity, and markdown exposure across 1,300 SKUs
  • Vendor scorecards on cost, accuracy, and reliability
  • Ad hoc deep-dives for ownership: spend reviews, pricing scenarios, whatever needs answering that week

Requirements

Requirements

  • 3 to 6 years in accounting or accounting plus FP&A, with real inventory, AP, or cost accounting exposure. Apparel, CPG, or DTC ecommerce strongly preferred
  • Fluent in 3-way matching and comfortable pushing back on vendors when the numbers do not add up
  • Excel killer: pivots, lookups, and models built from scratch
  • You think in unit economics, not just journal entries
  • ERP experience such as NetSuite, QuickBooks, or similar. Shopify ecosystem familiarity is a plus
  • Self-directed and fast

Benefits

  • Work From Anywhere

About Centric Software:

Centric Software® is a global leader, providing an innovative and AI-enabled product-concept-to-commercialization platform for retailers, brands and manufacturers of all sizes. We equip retail, fashion, luxury, footwear, outdoor, home and consumer goods brands with pioneering best-of-breed solutions to plan, design, develop, source, comply, buy, make, price, allocate, sell and replenish products. Our technology powers brands to streamline processes, drive efficiency and operate with confidence in an ever-changing market.

Our story is one of rapid growth, bold ideas and extraordinary opportunities. We’re here to challenge the status quo—and we’re looking for brilliant people who want to do the same. No matter where you are in the world, this is your chance to be part of something exceptional.

PURPOSE:

Generate and increase revenues in targeted geographic territory (South Korea) as well as named vertical accounts through direct sales activities presenting Product Intelligence Retail Solutions focused on the Fashion and Apparel Industry and/or Global Product Sourcing for the fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) market.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Ownership of revenue generation within assigned territory, as well as the quality & strength of the executive relationships within the territory.
  • Responsible for in-depth, broad-based sales presentations of the entire Centric PLM/Planning/Market Intelligence Solution suites.
  • Drive complex solution sales cycles to deal closure.
  • Prospect with qualified leads to identify business opportunities in which the Centric PLM/Planning/Market Intelligence Solution suite can provide business solutions.
  • Analyze customer business requirements as a basis to develop a sales strategy and propose Product Intelligence Solutions.
  • Produce written proposals & quotations.
  • Prepare business response documentation for RFI/RFP/RFQ requests.
  • Analyze requirements and design solutions to complex customer business requirements.
  • Working with a technical team, ensure clear understanding of customer’s technology requirements; provide sales leadership for Proposal and Project teams and vision to win and deliver large-scale, complex solutions.
  • Meet and exceed assigned revenue goals.
  • Develop and manage business plan for assigned territory
  • Participate in regional & national trade shows, exhibits and conferences.

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • 5+ years of proven success selling PLM/Planning/Market Intelligence and/or related Enterprise Application software.
  • Proven track record of consistently meeting and exceeded annual quotas.
  • Excellent presentation skills at executive level with small or large audiences.
  • Proven new account development skills and experience.
  • Confident and multi-level communication skills (oral and written)
  • Expertise or domain knowledge of Fashion & Apparel and/or FMCG market.
  • Experience preparing presentation materials and RFI/RFP responses.
  • Ability to develop multi-level relationships of confidence and trust with customers and cross-functional colleagues.
  • Ability to adapt to a rapidly evolving technology and commercial environment.
  • Proven experience selling software solutions that result in contracts in excess of $200,000.
